correctness.rationale: For chi<1, the stationary stiffness average is K>0; the two-sided convolution converges conditionally on the chain. Coupling two candidate stationary starts with the same chain state and the same future noises contracts their Y difference, proving uniqueness without a moment assumption. Reversibility and the Gaussian conditional variance give the integral of exp(-sH), H=2diag(K+phi)-Q. Its smallest eigenmode is strictly positive by irreducibility, so no stationary-state coordinate can avoid divergence when the smallest eigenvalue is nonpositive, including zero. The opposite-state difference mode for psi has eigenvalue 2(K+2lambda) in H. The remaining block of H/2 has pivots K+lambda and K+alpha with Schur complement K+alpha-A/(K+lambda)-alpha^2/(K+alpha), whose sign is B. Directly solving Hw=D1 yields w=DN/(2B) for each nonreciprocal state. Qpsi=-2lambda psi and phi psi=0 give covariance A w exp(-(K+2lambda)|t|)/2 for the propulsion drift, not for the white-noise part. Twice the triangular covariance integral plus Dt gives the stated variance. B at alpha=0 and lambda gives the two strength boundaries; the quotient derivative has numerator D A[K(K+lambda)-A]/2 and at the interior pole KN=A alpha_c, giving exactly the residue stated. For B<=0 the no-jump event in a nonreciprocal state leaves a nonzero multiple of the heavy-tailed Y_0 plus independent finite-variance noise at each t>0, so the raw second moment is infinite (a finite mean is not asserted). At chi=1 with a<K, bounded positive damping suffices in both closed classes; the nonreciprocal class has E[Y^2]=2D/K, the reciprocal drift vanishes, and w tends to D/(2K) from chi<1, giving the specified class average. The packaged script was inspected, not executed; the proof provides the parameter-uniform checks.
